content.text: {"headline":"Approve P2: chat deflection plus callback lifts the 12:45-19:45 window to 83.4% service level for ₹1,296","why":"Payments calls are running about 24.5% above forecast (1524 vs 1224.5 today) with no outage, incident or campaign to explain it, and every call reason is up. With no action the window is predicted at 78.1% (payments 72.4%), below the 80% target. P2 deflects 20% of refund_status and payment_status_enquiry calls to chat over the two pressure periods (12:45-15:00 and 18:00-20:00), adds IVR callback 13:00-15:00 and delays payments breaks by 45 minutes. This brings the window to 83.4% overall and cuts abandons from 5.3% to 4.3%. It is the cheapest policy-compliant plan that reaches target. Escalation is not required.","trade_offs":["P1 (₹750) is cheaper but makes things worse: 76.7% overall, 70.1% on payments, 5.9% abandons.","P3 (₹6,480, 87.6%) and P4 (₹5,616, 91.3%, payments 90.0%) give more headroom but cost roughly 4-5x more and depend on agents accepting overtime.","Payments itself is predicted at 79.3% under P2, just under 80%. The overall target is met because general holds at 90.7%. P2 moves no agents off general, so there is no risk to that queue.","Chat deflection asks some customers to switch channels, so chat volumes will rise during the deflection windows."],"watch":"Check payments service level and chat backlog through 13:00-15:00. If the surge keeps growing, or payments stays well below 80%, be ready to add overtime as in P4. Payments has the least margin of the two queues."}
